_comment: THE SHARED GATE CORPUS. Ticket 03 ruling 2's actual deliverable.
Ruling 2 accepted TWO implementations of the same reconciliation arithmetic - a Kotlin
pre-check on the phone and the SQL inside the commit RPCs - on one condition: that something
proves they agree. This file is that something. It is the single source of truth for what the
gate must do, and both sides are checked against it rather than against each other.
Every case states its own arithmetic explicitly so a reader can verify the expectation by
hand. If a case's `expect` disagrees with its own numbers, the case is wrong, not the code.
tools/gate_corpus_sql.py                                     (emits SQL for the RPC side)
WHAT THIS DOES NOT YET COVER, stated so its absence is not mistaken for coverage: the phone's
own pre-check does not exist yet (ticket 03 ruling 2 specifies it; the CSV import path that
would host it is unbuilt). Until it does, the Kotlin side here verifies the ARITHMETIC each
case asserts, which is the same arithmetic both implementations must produce. When the
pre-check lands it plugs into the same corpus and the comparison becomes direct.

ledger.name: empty extraction quarantines even when every figure is zero
ledger.why: RULE 6. sum of no rows is 0, and closing - opening is 0, so BOTH anchors are satisfied by nothing at all. This is how a card statement once passed with four dropped interest rows, and it only held because interest was zero that month. The non-empty check must run BEFORE the arithmetic.

ledger.name: lines that do not sum to the stated total quarantine
balance movement disagreeing with the line sum quarantines
ledger.why: sum = 149550 and stated = 149550, so anchor 1 PASSES. But closing - opening = 1 - 500000, which does not. This is the case a single-anchor gate would wave through, and the reason ruling 4 requires three printed figures rather than one.

ledger.name: a single line that ties out commits
ledger.why: The degenerate but legal case. sum = -899 = stated; 99101 - 100000 = -899.

ledger.name: a genuinely zero-movement month with a real line commits
ledger.why: Guards against over-correcting rule 6 into refusing legitimate zero sums. Two lines that cancel: sum = 0 = stated, and closing equals opening. There IS an extraction here, so the gate must accept it.

ledger.name: deterministic two-anchor statement with no printed total commits
ledger.why: AMENDMENT (ticket 12, RULED 2026-08-27). stated_total_cents is null because this bank prints none. provenance is DETERMINISTIC, so anchor 1 is skipped. Anchor 2 still holds: 649550 - 500000 = 149550 = sum(-450, 300000, -150000).

ledger.name: deterministic two-anchor statement whose delta check fails quarantines
ledger.why: Same shape as the case above, but closing_balance_cents is wrong: 1 - 500000 does not equal the line sum of 149550. With no stated total to check, anchor 2 is the ONLY anchor left, and it must still be enforced.

ledger.name: LLM-reconciled statement missing its stated total quarantines (the amendment's scope guard)
ledger.why: The load-bearing half of the 2026-08-27 amendment: the two-anchor allowance is scoped to DETERMINISTIC extraction only. This statement has no stated_total_cents but is LLM_RECONCILED, so it is refused outright even though its balance delta ties out (649550 - 500000 = 149550 = sum).

ledger.name: deterministic statement with no printed total and zero lines still quarantines under rule 6
ledger.why: RULE 6, in the new no-total shape. With stated_total_cents null, provenance DETERMINISTIC, and zero lines, sum is 0 and closing - opening is 0, so anchor 2 alone would be satisfied by nothing at all if the empty check did not run first.

pantry.name: valid receipt with a printed subtotal commits
pantry.why: items 450 + 700 = 1150 = subtotal. subtotal 1150 + tax 92 + other 0 = 1242 = total. Both anchors hold.

pantry.name: items not summing to the printed subtotal quarantines
pantry.why: ANCHOR 1. items = 1150, subtotal claims 1300. An item was probably not read.

pantry.name: subtotal plus tax not reaching the printed total quarantines
pantry.why: ANCHOR 2. items tie to the subtotal, but 1150 + 92 = 1242, not the 9999 printed.

pantry.name: no printed subtotal, figures tie, commits
pantry.why: THE COLLAPSE CASE. With no subtotal the two anchors become one: items 1150 + tax 92 = 1242 = total.

pantry.name: no printed subtotal, figures do not tie, quarantines
pantry.why: The other half of the collapse. Without this case a bug that always accepted the no-subtotal branch would pass the corpus.

pantry.name: macro estimates never affect the gate
pantry.why: SECTION 4 RULE 5. A receipt never prints calories, so they are a model's guess and are excluded from every anchor. These figures are deliberately absurd; the case must still commit on its money alone.
